newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest BUX edges up to new high in huge turnover.
newsitem.headline: Budapest BUX edges up to new high in huge turnover.

text.p: Hungarian shares closed mixed in pre-Christmas trade on Monday as they followed trends on European markets, traders said.
"The market's recent rising trend lost steam," said Tamas Revesz of Wintrust Securities (formerly called AEB Securities).
Nevertheless, early gains by some of the market's leading stocks helped the BUX index to extend its recent gains and close at a successive new high of 4,102.47 points, up 5.95.

In early trade some key Hungarian stocks, including oil company MOL, chemical firms TVK and Borsodchem and hotelier Danubius hit new record highs but strong gains reached in the past few days urged many investors to lock in profits.
"There's profit-taking on the market as people may have overshot their targets," a salesman said. "Last week's euphory is followed by sobering, even if sobering comes in waves."
Spot share turnover of 3.70 billion was the highest since the record 5.77 billion reached on August 1, 1995.
Pharmaceuticals Richter alone generated a turnover of 1.475 billion forints, boosted by an agency cross for 122,000 stocks at 9,080 forints. Richter ended at 9,380 forints, down 20.
In an agency cross the same securities house matches a buy and a sell orders from different clients.
Borsodchem finished at 4,055 forints, up five, but below a new record of 4,080. TVK closed at 1,845, down 25 and below the new high of 1,895.
The Budapest Stock Exchange will reopen on December 30.
